# Plugin quickstart

Three minimal plugin shapes, generated from checked fixtures under `scripts/plugin-api-docs/tutorial-fixtures/`. Their manifests are validated when `bun run docs:plugin-api` runs.

## Development loop

Start with a scaffold when developing from the HAPI source tree:

```bash
bun run plugin:create -- com.example.my-plugin --template hub-notification
bun run plugin:validate -- plugins/com.example.my-plugin
bun run plugin:pack -- plugins/com.example.my-plugin --out /tmp/com.example.my-plugin.tgz
hapi plugins install-package /tmp/com.example.my-plugin.tgz --dry-run --json
```

For ad-hoc external directories, write `hapi.plugin.json` and optional runtime files, then install locally:

```bash
mkdir -p my-plugin/dist
# write hapi.plugin.json and optional runtime files
hapi plugins install-local ./my-plugin --target hub --enable --reload
hapi plugins list --target hub
hapi plugins inspect <plugin-id> --target hub
hapi plugins doctor <plugin-id>
```

For Runner plugins, replace `--target hub` with `--target runner:<machineId>` or use manifest-driven package install:

```bash
hapi plugins install-package ./my-plugin.hapi-plugin.tgz --runners compatible --enable --reload
```


## Tutorial: Hub notification plugin

Build a Hub runtime plugin that receives HAPI notification events and logs them.

Create `hapi.plugin.json`:

```json
{
    "id": "com.example.tutorial.notification-logger",
    "name": "Tutorial Notification Logger",
    "version": "0.1.0",
    "pluginApiVersion": "0.1",
    "description": "A tutorial Hub plugin that logs HAPI notification events.",
    "runtimes": {
        "hub": {
            "entry": "dist/hub.js"
        }
    },
    "contributions": {
        "hub": {
            "notificationChannels": [
                {
                    "id": "tutorial-logger",
                    "displayName": "Tutorial Logger"
                }
            ]
        },
        "web": {
            "settingsPanels": [
                {
                    "id": "tutorial-notification-logger",
                    "title": "Tutorial Notification Logger",
                    "description": "Configure the prefix used by the tutorial notification logger.",
                    "components": [
                        {
                            "kind": "text",
                            "text": "This Hub runtime plugin logs notification events."
                        },
                        {
                            "kind": "schemaForm",
                            "title": "Logger options",
                            "fields": [
                                {
                                    "key": "prefix",
                                    "label": "Log prefix",
                                    "type": "text",
                                    "defaultValue": "[tutorial-plugin]"
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ]
                }
            ]
        }
    },
    "permissions": {
        "network": ["https://example.com/*"],
        "secrets": ["TUTORIAL_WEBHOOK_TOKEN"]
    }
}
```

Create `dist/hub.js`:

```js
export function activate(ctx) {
    const prefix = String(ctx.config.get('prefix') ?? '[tutorial-plugin]')
    const token = ctx.secrets.get('TUTORIAL_WEBHOOK_TOKEN')

    ctx.logger.info('Tutorial notification logger activated. tokenPresent=%s', Boolean(token))

    ctx.notifications.registerChannel({
        async send(event) {
            ctx.logger.info(
                `${prefix} type=${event.type} session=${event.session.id} agent=${event.session.agent ?? 'unknown'}`
            )
        },

        async dispose() {
            ctx.logger.info('Tutorial notification logger disposed.')
        }
    })
}
```

Install:

```bash
hapi plugins install-local ./hub-notification --target hub --enable --reload
```

Hub-local path install reads files on the Hub machine.

## Tutorial: Runner environment plugin

Build a Runner runtime plugin that injects environment variables and spawn diagnostics.

Create `hapi.plugin.json`:

```json
{
    "id": "com.example.tutorial.runner-env",
    "name": "Tutorial Runner Environment",
    "version": "0.1.0",
    "pluginApiVersion": "0.1",
    "description": "A tutorial Runner plugin that injects an environment variable and records spawn diagnostics.",
    "runtimes": {
        "runner": {
            "entry": "dist/runner.js"
        }
    },
    "contributions": {
        "runner": {
            "environmentProviders": [
                {
                    "id": "tutorial-env",
                    "displayName": "Tutorial Environment Provider"
                }
            ],
            "spawnHooks": [
                {
                    "id": "tutorial-spawn-audit",
                    "displayName": "Tutorial Spawn Audit"
                }
            ]
        },
        "web": {
            "settingsPanels": [
                {
                    "id": "tutorial-runner-env",
                    "title": "Tutorial Runner Environment",
                    "components": [
                        {
                            "kind": "text",
                            "text": "Enable this plugin on a Runner target to add TUTORIAL_RUNNER_ENV to spawned agents."
                        },
                        {
                            "kind": "schemaForm",
                            "title": "Environment options",
                            "fields": [
                                {
                                    "key": "envValue",
                                    "label": "Environment value",
                                    "type": "text",
                                    "defaultValue": "enabled"
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ]
                }
            ]
        }
    }
}
```

Create `dist/runner.js`:

```js
export function activate(ctx) {
    const envValue = String(ctx.config.get('envValue') ?? 'enabled')

    ctx.runtime.registerEnvironmentProvider({
        id: 'tutorial-env',
        priority: 10,
        provide(context) {
            return {
                env: {
                    TUTORIAL_RUNNER_ENV: envValue
                },
                diagnostics: [{
                    severity: 'info',
                    code: 'tutorial-env-applied',
                    message: `Tutorial env applied for ${context.agent}`
                }]
            }
        }
    })

    ctx.runtime.registerSpawnHook({
        id: 'tutorial-spawn-audit',
        priority: 10,
        beforeSpawn(context) {
            return {
                diagnostics: [{
                    severity: 'info',
                    code: 'tutorial-spawn-audit',
                    message: `Tutorial plugin observed ${context.agent} spawn in ${context.cwd}`
                }]
            }
        }
    })
}
```

Install:

```bash
hapi plugins install-local ./runner-env --target runner:<machineId> --enable --reload
```

Runner-local path install reads files on the selected Runner machine; use package install when Hub and Runner are on different machines.

## Tutorial: Web descriptor plugin

Build a descriptor-only plugin rendered by the Web UI without browser-side plugin JavaScript.

Create `hapi.plugin.json`:

```json
{
    "id": "com.example.tutorial.web-descriptor",
    "name": "Tutorial Web Descriptor",
    "version": "0.1.0",
    "pluginApiVersion": "0.1",
    "description": "A descriptor-only tutorial plugin rendered by the Web UI without executing plugin JavaScript.",
    "contributions": {
        "web": {
            "settingsPanels": [
                {
                    "id": "tutorial-web-panel",
                    "title": "Tutorial Web Descriptor",
                    "description": "Descriptor-only settings panel.",
                    "components": [
                        {
                            "kind": "text",
                            "text": "This plugin has no runtime entry. Web renders this validated descriptor only.",
                            "tone": "info"
                        },
                        {
                            "kind": "badge",
                            "label": "Descriptor only",
                            "variant": "success"
                        },
                        {
                            "kind": "schemaForm",
                            "title": "Descriptor config",
                            "fields": [
                                {
                                    "key": "note",
                                    "label": "Note",
                                    "type": "text",
                                    "defaultValue": "hello from descriptor"
                                }
                            ]
                        }
                    ]
                }
            ],
            "newSessionFields": [
                {
                    "id": "tutorial-session-note",
                    "key": "tutorialNote",
                    "label": "Tutorial note",
                    "type": "text",
                    "defaultValue": "descriptor-field"
                }
            ],
            "actions": [
                {
                    "id": "reload-self",
                    "label": "Reload plugin",
                    "actionId": "plugin.reload"
                }
            ],
            "badges": [
                {
                    "id": "tutorial-descriptor",
                    "label": "Tutorial",
                    "variant": "success"
                }
            ]
        }
    }
}
```

Install:

```bash
hapi plugins install-local ./web-descriptor --target hub --enable --reload
```

Hub-local path install reads files on the Hub machine.

## Safety checklist

- Hub and Runner runtime plugins are trusted local in-process JavaScript.
- Disabled or invalid runtime plugins are not imported.
- Secrets are read from environment variables through `ctx.secrets.get(name)` and must not be saved in `plugins.json`.
- Network requests should use `ctx.network.fetch`; `permissions.network` is a basic SDK allow-list check, not a sandbox.
- Web contributions are descriptors only; Web does not execute plugin JavaScript.
